verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, according to the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve as my forefathers did, with a pure conscience. How unceasing is my memory of you in my petitions, night and day
longing to see you, remembering your tears, that I may be filled with joy;
having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you; which lived first in your grandmother Lois, and your mother Eunice, and, I am persuaded, in you also.
For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,
who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News.
For this, I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this cause I also suffer these things. Yet I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day.
Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
That good thing which was committed to you, guard through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
This you know, that all who are in Asia turned away from me; of whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord grant mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain,
but when he was in Rome, he sought me diligently, and found me
(the Lord grant to him to find the Lord’s mercy in that day); and in how many things he served at Ephesus, you know very well.

footnotes.content: Paul opens by claiming his authority through Christ—not earned, but chosen. Watch how he speaks: apostle, through God's will, by the promise of life itself. He stakes everything on Jesus being the Author, the Caller. That's where any faithful word begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To Timothy, beloved. That word—beloved—is not sentiment; it's covenant. Grace, mercy, peace. Paul blesses the young man not with gold, but with the very nature of God. When you are overwhelmed, a word like this, spoken truly, can hold you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul prays for Timothy constantly—night and day. He serves as his fathers did, with a clean conscience. This is the rhythm of faithfulness: remember before God, with a clear heart. The prayers never stop; they are the work beneath the work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Longing to see you, remembering your tears. Paul remembers Timothy weeping—his heart, his struggles. This is pastoral love: specific, embodied, not abstract. He longs for the young man's presence, his laughter, his restored joy. The pastor's hunger for his flock's wholeness runs deep.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Faith lived first in Lois, then Eunice, now Timothy. Three generations, unbroken. Paul sees the lineage—grandmother, mother, son—and names it with wonder. That's how the kingdom moves: through mothers and grandmothers who will not bend. Do you know who bore you into faith?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stir up the gift. It's already there—Paul reminds Timothy through the laying on of hands—but it can lie dormant, banked like embers. The Lord gave it; now Timothy must act. We are not passive in our own transformation; we tend what God has lit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not a spirit of fear, but power, love, self-control. When you are small and young and the world is large, you feel the fear rising. But Paul says no—the Spirit inside you is not timid. It is mighty, it is gentle, it is sane. We forget this when the voice of dread gets loud.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't be ashamed of the testimony or of Paul his prisoner. In Rome, chains. But Paul, shackled, still stands as a witness. Timothy will face pressure to hide, to go silent—the same pressure every faithful heart knows. Courage is not the absence of fear; it is speaking when silence is easier.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Called with a holy calling, not by our works but His purpose and grace—given in Christ before time began. Predestination, some call it. The weight of this: you are not accident, not afterthought. Grounded before the foundation, known, loved, called. That's your foundation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Death abolished. Life and immortality brought to light. Jesus didn't just defeat death in the future—He revealed it as already undone when He rose. The Good News announces what is true: the tomb is empty, and you are free. That's the message Paul asks Timothy to carry.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul was made preacher, apostle, teacher. A calling. Not every heart is called to stand in the pulpit, but every believer is called to speak. Timothy is learning from Paul how to open your mouth and say: This is true. Jesus is Lord. Do you bear witness where you stand?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I suffer, yet I am not ashamed—for I know Him whom I have believed. Not abstract doctrine; I know Him. And I trust He guards what I've given Him. When hardship comes, your only anchor is intimate knowledge of Jesus' character. That intimacy is forged in the long watching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hold the pattern of sound words from Paul—in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus. A pattern: right doctrine held in the warmth of faith and love. Not a frozen creed, but a living shape. Hold it as a beloved holds a precious thing—carefully, because it is true and beautiful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Guard the deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. Not by your strength alone—the Spirit indwells you, guards you as you guard the faith. It's mutual: you stand, He sustains. The treasure is not fragile; it is held by the one who made all things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All in Asia turned away. Phygelus and Hermogenes—named. When friends desert, it stings. Paul doesn't hide the wound. Yet he doesn't linger there either. Some will fall away; that is the nature of the world. Your task is not to hold everyone—it is to hold fast yourself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Onesiphorus, who refreshed Paul in chains and was not ashamed of them. One faithful friend. In the loneliest hour, one person showed up. Such a small thing—to visit a prisoner—and such an enormous thing. Do you know someone waiting in darkness, praying a friend will come?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He sought diligently and found Paul in Rome. Imagine the search—through a great city, into the prison system, to locate one suffering friend. That is the love that does not give up. It looks, it searches, it shows up. Onesiphorus did not calculate the cost; he simply went.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord grant him to find the Lord's mercy in that day. Readers today hear an echo here: we too are seeking mercy. Onesiphorus' faithful feet, his courage to show up for a chained man, these are what mercy looks like embodied. As of 2026-10, we still need such faithfulness—still need to find each other in the darkness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
